text:
Line 3 of `catalog/members.py`, quoted exactly:

> `# The lending policy allows each member to hold five books at once.`

The constant on line 4 was `MAX_BORROWED = 3`, which contradicted that comment. That was one of six bugs. After the fixes below, `python3 -m unittest` passes all 16 tests. Before, it showed 15, because `test_search` couldn't be imported. I didn't change any tests.

- **`catalog/members.py:4`**: changed `MAX_BORROWED` from 3 to 5, to match the comment and the tests.
- **`catalog/search.py:3`**: the import pointed at a module that doesn't exist, `catalog.nonexistent`. It now imports `normalize` from `catalog.text`.
- **`catalog/books.py:22`**: `parse_book` now turns the year into an integer with `int(year)`. This fixes both `test_year_is_int` and `test_age`.
- **`catalog/fees.py:14`**: the fee was days late *plus* the daily fee; it's now days late *times* the daily fee.
- **`catalog/inventory.py:24`**: `recent(n)` was returning one event too many. It now uses `self._history[-n:]`, and returns an empty list when `n <= 0`.
- **`catalog/factory.py`**: added the missing `Book("Emma", "Austen", 1815, 1)` to `sample_books()`. The tests only check the title, so I chose the author, year and copy count myself.
